chunks: Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام said regarding a man who is owed money by another man and asks him for repayment, but he does not have what he can repay with, so he says, "It remains with you as a muḍārabah investment." He said: "It is not valid until he takes possession of it from him."

key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not valid or proper in legal effect
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or money owed in the case under discussion

ai.seo_question: Can a debt be treated directly as a muḍārabah investment without first taking possession of the money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a debt being converted into a muḍārabah investment arrangement. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام states that such an arrangement is not valid unless the creditor first takes possession of the owed amount from the debtor.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3845 - Al-Sakooni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said regarding a man who is owed money by another man and demands repayment, but the debtor does not have the means to repay and says, "Consider it as a partnership investment with you."
Imam (as) said: "It is not permissible until he first takes possession of it from him."
